activities.title: Room Repeater: first words in English
steps: Room Repeater is a separate picture-and-word game for ages 1.5 to 4.
Your child taps a picture, hears the word and tries to say it. You sit close and cheer.
One short session a day is plenty.
activities.why: A few playful minutes with new words, side by side with you.

sources.title: Room Repeater

activities.title: Sock pairs
steps: Put 4 to 6 pairs of clean socks in a pile on the floor.
Hold one up and name its colour: "A blue sock. Where's the other blue one?"
Cheer each pair you find together, then swap roles.
activities.why: Matching and naming colours together builds early thinking and new words, with you as the play partner.

sources.title: Positive Parenting Tips: Toddlers (1–2 years old)
Baby and toddler play ideas

activities.title: Little kitchen helper
steps: Give a safe job: washing big vegetables in a bowl of water, or stirring with a wooden spoon.
Describe what you both do: "We wash the carrot. Splash!"
Stay within arm's reach, and keep knives, hot pans and small bits of food away.
activities.why: Copying you with real tasks helps toddlers feel part of the family and brings lots of new words.

sources.title: Positive Parenting Tips: Toddlers (1–2 years old)
Milestones by 18 Months

activities.title: Teddy's picnic
steps: Sit a teddy and a doll on a blanket with plastic cups and plates.
Offer teddy a pretend drink, then pass the cup on: "Would teddy like some too?"
Follow your child's idea, even if teddy suddenly goes to sleep.
activities.why: Pretend play with simple props lets many toddlers try out everyday life and take turns with you.

sources.title: Milestones by 18 Months
Positive Parenting Tips: Toddlers (1–2 years old)

activities.title: Treasure walk
steps: Take a bag or basket to a park or courtyard.
Collect big treasures together: large leaves, pine cones, sticks longer than your hand.
Name each one and compare: "Big leaf, small leaf." Make sure nothing goes in the mouth.
activities.why: Exploring outdoors with you feeds curiosity and gives you lots to talk about.

sources.title: Positive Parenting Tips: Toddlers (1–2 years old)
Physical activity guidelines for children (under 5 years)

activities.title: Copy me
steps: Find a safe grassy spot away from the road.
Walk, stomp, tiptoe or crouch, and invite your child to copy you.
Swap: now you copy them, and make a big deal of their moves.
activities.why: Moving together builds balance, and taking turns to lead shows your child that their ideas count.

sources.title: Milestones by 18 Months
Physical activity guidelines for children (under 5 years)

activities.title: Puddle stomp (rainy days)
steps: After rain, put on wellies and waterproofs. Spring and autumn are ideal.
Hold hands and stomp into a shallow puddle together: one, two, three, splash!
Stay within arm's reach and skip puddles near the road.
activities.why: Big, joyful movements and a shared laugh are a simple way to connect, and wet boots are part of the fun.

sources.title: Positive Parenting Tips: Toddlers (1–2 years old)
Physical activity guidelines for children (under 5 years)

activities.title: Feelings faces
steps: Sit face to face, or together in front of a mirror.
Make a happy, sad, surprised or cross face and name it: "This is my sad face."
Now your child makes a face and you guess the feeling.
activities.why: Naming feelings in play gives many children words for what they feel, and shows every feeling is welcome with you.

sources.title: Milestones by 2 Years
Positive Parenting Tips: Toddlers (2–3 years old)

activities.title: Cosy den
steps: Turn a big cardboard box on its side, or drape a blanket over two chairs.
Crawl in together with a book or a teddy and read in your den.
Take turns inviting guests: "Knock knock, who's there?"
activities.why: A small den is a cosy place for closeness and pretend play, and many two-year-olds love being "inside".

sources.title: Milestones by 30 Months
Positive Parenting Tips: Toddlers (2–3 years old)

activities.title: Tidy-up song
steps: Pick a short tune and sing: "Blocks go in the box, in the box…"
Put one toy away yourself, then hand one to your child.
Celebrate the end with a high five.
activities.why: Simple requests set to a song turn tidying into a shared game rather than a battle.

sources.title: Milestones by 30 Months
Positive Parenting Tips: Toddlers (2–3 years old)

activities.title: Kick and chase
steps: Take a big soft ball to a park or courtyard, away from the road.
Kick it gently to each other, then chase it together.
Cheer every try, not just the goals.
activities.why: Kicking and running build strength and coordination, and cheering the effort shows you enjoy playing together.

sources.title: Milestones by 2 Years
Physical activity guidelines for children (under 5 years)

activities.title: Colour hunt
steps: Pick one colour for the walk, for example red.
Point out everything red you spot: a car, a door, a flower. Hold hands near the road.
Let your child choose the colour for the next round.
activities.why: Spotting things together turns an ordinary walk into a game full of words and pointing.

sources.title: Milestones by 30 Months
Positive Parenting Tips: Toddlers (2–3 years old)

activities.title: Jump the line
steps: Find a line on a park path, or draw one in the sandpit with your finger.
Show a two-foot jump over the line, then hold hands and jump together.
Count the jumps, or make animal sounds as you land.
activities.why: Jumping with both feet is a new skill for many children around this age, and doing it with you makes it brave and fun.

sources.title: Milestones by 30 Months
Physical activity guidelines for children (under 5 years)

activities.title: Story in turns
steps: Start a story with one sentence: "One day, a hedgehog found a key…"
Take turns adding one sentence each.
At the end ask: "What happened first? And then?"
activities.why: Building a story in turns practises telling events in order and listening, and many four-year-olds love silly twists.

sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
Positive Parenting Tips: Preschoolers (3–5 years old)

activities.title: Funny-face sandwich plate
steps: Wash hands together and set out bread, a soft spread and a few vegetables.
Let your child spread with a blunt knife and arrange a face on the plate.
Eat it together and talk about the best part of the day.
activities.why: Real kitchen jobs build independence and fine motor skills, and sharing the result is a moment of closeness.

sources.title: Positive Parenting Tips: Preschoolers (3–5 years old)
Milestones by 4 Years

activities.title: Your own board game
steps: Draw a winding path of 15 squares on paper, with a start and a finish.
Use a die and two bottle caps as pieces.
Agree on one special rule together, like "land on a star, jump once".
activities.why: Games with turns and rules practise waiting, counting and coping with losing, which is easiest with a calm grown-up.

sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
Positive Parenting Tips: Preschoolers (3–5 years old)

activities.title: Hop trail
steps: In a park, mark a trail with sticks or leaves: hop, jump, walk on tiptoe.
Take turns choosing the next move.
Try hopping on one foot, holding hands if that helps.
activities.why: Hopping and balancing build strength and confidence, and taking turns gives your child a say in the game.

sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
Physical activity guidelines for children (under 5 years)

activities.title: Question walk
steps: On a walk, take turns asking "why" and "how" questions: "Why do leaves fall?"
Guess the answers together before anyone explains.
Hold hands when you cross a road.
activities.why: Wondering aloud together shows that questions are welcome, and builds language and reasoning.

sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
Positive Parenting Tips: Preschoolers (3–5 years old)
Child development

activities.title: Shadow tag (sunny days)
steps: On a sunny day, find an open space in a park or courtyard, away from the road.
Try to step on each other's shadows, then make shadow shapes together.
Notice how shadows are long in the morning and evening and short at midday.
activities.why: Running games with simple rules bring energy and laughter, and shadows spark curiosity about the world.
